newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-SERGI BRUGUERA CARVES UP BYRON BLACK IN NEW HAVEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SERGI BRUGUERA CARVES UP BYRON BLACK IN NEW HAVEN.

text.p: Second-seeded
Sergi Bruguera of Spain carved up Byron Black of Zimbabwe 6-3
6-2 in a second-round match on a rain-abbreviated day at the
Pilot Pen tennis tournament Wednesday.
Bruguera, a two-time French Open champion whose world
ranking last year dropped below the top 20 for the first time
since 1990, was always in command against Black, better known
for his doubles accomplishments.
Bruguera, a clay-court specialist, made 65 percent of his
first serves and never lost his delivery in the match on New
Haven's hard surface.
"I've been trying to serve better and play more
aggressively on hard courts," he said. "I don't serve that
hard but I can mix it up.
Bruguera already has been in four finals this year, two on
hard courts.
"I'm moving better and I'm relaxed mentally. And I know
when I'm playing my best tennis I can win on this surface."
Also advancing was fourth-seeded Richard Krajicek of the
Netherlands, who had little trouble dispatching Nicolas
Lapenti of Ecuador 6-4 6-3.
Krajicek, owner of one of the most powerful services in
the game, had his weapon working with authority and was never
in trouble in the match.
In the first match of the day, which started at 4:45 p.m.,
Spain's Javier Sanchez used his backcourt consistency and
superior speed to outlast Paul Haarhuis of the Netherlands 3-6
At 3-all in the third set, Sanchez broke his opponent's
service in the seventh and ninth games to run out the match.
"I was tired in the third set, the humidity bothered me,"
said Haarhuis.
Only three of a scheduled 18 matches reached completion.
Two matches which were started on non-stadium courts were
suspended in the third set because of darkness.
American Vince Spadea led Slava Dosedel of Czechoslovakia,
5-7 6-3 3-1 and Brett Steven of New Zealand and Dinu Piscariu
of Romania were tied at 3-3 in the third set. Steven won the
first set 6-4 and Pescariu took the second set 6-0.
